sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Emergency Management
sections.description: This section walks the learner through the patient’s initial signs, symptoms, and vital findings, and details the step‑by‑step emergency interventions that were applied according to current anaphylaxis protocols.
subtopics: Brief patient profile and relevant comorbidities
Timeline of drug exposure (clarithromycin) and symptom onset
Recognition of anaphylaxis: airway, breathing, circulation, cutaneous criteria
Initial vital signs and physical examination findings
First‑line pharmacologic treatment: intramuscular epinephrine dosing, antihistamine (clemastine) use, oxygen therapy, fluid resuscitation
Rationale for choosing a 0.3 mg auto‑injector versus weight‑based dosing
Immediate response to therapy and criteria for response assessment

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Anaphylaxis and Underlying Mast Cell Disorders
sections.description: Provides the immunologic and cellular mechanisms that drive anaphylaxis, focusing on IgE‑mediated mast cell/basophil activation, and introduces systemic mastocytosis as a predisposing condition that can amplify reactions and promote biphasic/multiphasic courses.
subtopics: IgE‑mediated versus non‑IgE pathways in drug‑induced anaphylaxis
Mediators released by mast cells (histamine, tryptase, leukotrienes, prostaglandins) and their clinical effects
Definition and WHO criteria for systemic mastocytosis (major and minor criteria)
How increased mast cell burden influences severity, recurrence, and tryptase dynamics
Interaction of clarithromycin with mast cell activation (possible hapten formation)
Risk factors for biphasic/multiphasic anaphylaxis (delay in epinephrine, severity of index reaction, underlying mast cell disease)

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Work‑up and Reasoning: From Acute Phase to Follow‑up
sections.description: Explains the laboratory and imaging investigations performed, the timing of serum tryptase sampling, interpretation of results, and the decision‑making process regarding allergy testing and mastocytosis work‑up.
subtopics: Guideline‑recommended timing of tryptase measurements (acute, 1‑4 h, baseline ≥24 h) and interpretation of elevated levels
Analysis of the case’s tryptase values and what they suggest about mast cell activation
Bone marrow biopsy considerations and why major criteria could not be assessed
Role and limitation of skin testing or drug provocation in severe reactions
Differential diagnosis: distinguishing true biphasic recurrence from persistent/refractory anaphylaxis
Use of adjunct investigations (abdominal ultrasound for hepatomegaly, neuropsychiatric assessment) to support mastocytosis suspicion

sections.section_title: Management of Multiphasic Anaphylaxis: Strategies, Controversies, and Decision Points
sections.description: Analyzes the challenges of recurrent anaphylaxis, compares therapeutic options (repeat IM epinephrine, continuous IV epinephrine, corticosteroids), and outlines monitoring protocols derived from current evidence and guideline gaps.
subtopics: Definition of biphasic vs. multiphasic anaphylaxis and typical time frames
Review of each recurrence in the case: dose, route, clinical response, and trend of symptom severity
Evidence base for repeat IM epinephrine versus IV infusion in refractory or multiphasic cases
Controversy surrounding systemic corticosteroids: historical rationale, recent systematic reviews, and specific application in this patient
Observation period recommendations (4‑12 h, risk‑stratified models) and ICU versus ward placement criteria
Practical algorithm for clinicians facing a second or third reaction (early specialist consultation, consider mastocytosis, adjust epinephrine dosing)
Patient‑centered discharge planning: prescribing an auto‑injector, antihistamine therapy, education on avoidance and emergency action plan

sections.section_title: Clinical Lessons, Future Directions, and System‑Level Recommendations
sections.description: Summarizes key take‑aways for trainees, highlights gaps in evidence, and proposes systemic improvements such as registries and guideline refinements to better manage complex anaphylaxis cases.
subtopics: Key learning points: prompt epinephrine, awareness of under‑dosing, importance of repeat assessment
Recognition of mast cell disorders as hidden risk factors in atypical anaphylaxis courses
Critical appraisal of current guidelines on monitoring duration and steroid use
Proposed risk‑stratification tools incorporating severity, epinephrine dose count, and comorbid mastocytosis
Value of case registries for rare multiphasic reactions and how they can inform expert consensus
Areas for research: optimal epinephrine dosing in obese adults, prophylactic IV epinephrine, steroid efficacy, mastocytosis‑specific protocols
Practical checklist for emergency and inpatient teams when encountering multiphasic anaphylaxis
